I wrote the polyglot to `polyglot/main.rs`. It builds with both `rustc` and `g++ -x c++`, and both programs give the same answers for every value I tried.

| N | Output (both versions) |

**How it works:** the trick is that Rust lets block comments nest and C++ doesn't.
- The file starts with `/* /* */`. C++ treats that as one complete comment and goes on to read the C++ code. Rust sees two comments opened and only one closed, so it skips everything until the `// */` line.
- The Rust code sits inside `#if 0 … #endif`, so C++ skips it.
- At the end, `// \` followed by `/*` hides the `#endif` from Rust. In C++ the backslash joins the two lines into a single line comment, so the `#endif` still counts.

Both versions use the same arbitrary-precision addition (base 10⁹ chunks), so large N doesn't overflow. With no argument, they print f(0) = 1.
